records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 [roadway] 64 behind heavy traffic, slowed by an oversized load vehicle and its escort vehicle. directly ahead of the oversized load, a fedex truck parked in the flush median, with the operator (unit 2) preparing to deliver a package to the address of 16490 sh 64. operator of unit 1 became impatient, and decided to pass as much traffic as possible, despite the fact he was in a no passing zone. the no passing zone then turned into a flush median, which cannot be crossed according to texas transportation code 545. 063. operator of unit 1 continued, until he observed the fedex truck parked in the flush median. operator of unit 1 then vacated the flush median, and was traveling on the wrong side of the roadway. unit 2, seeing no oncoming traffic, then exited her vehicle to deliver the package. after stepping out, unit 2 was struck by unit 1's front right and was thrown a considerable distance into the flush median. unit 1 then struck three mailboxes with its left distributed before coming to rest on the [roadway]. unit 2 was transported to ut health and pronounced deceased at 2:04 p. m. by medical personnel; a subsequent autopsy did not detect the presence of drugs or alcohol. operator of unit 1 provided a voluntary breath sample on a pbt which did not detect the presence of alcohol. an assisting trooper administered a field sobriety test and determined operator of unit 1 was not intoxicated. during the investigation, this investigator noted that the fedex truck was illegally parked in the flush median, having violated texas transportation code sections 545. 063 and 545. 303. in this investigator's opinion, the crash was primarily caused by operator of unit 1's decision to pass in a no passing zone, with the illegal parking possibly contributing. it is possible unit 2 may still have been struck, even if her vehicle was legally parked on the east side of the roadway.

pedestrian. the caller reported that he pulled into his driveway and ran over a man who was laying in the callers driveway. upon arrival, desoto traffic ofc. v. gonzalez observed a black, later identified as landrum, ronald (pedestrian) laying on his side (left side) in the driveway of [roadway]. ronald was actively bleeding from his right foot. upon contact, ronald stated that he was conscious, calm and collected. he advised okay and was not feeling pain, but could not articulate what he was doing or what occurred. ronald, at some point, mentioned that he thought he in his driveway. contact was then made with the caller, later identified as toven, phillip (driver) who reported the following: he turned onto the [roadway]. he further explained that there was nobody on the sidewalk when he pulled into his driveway, however, as he drove through his driveway to get to his garage he felt two bumps. toven said he stopped and initially thought that he ran over a dog/animal but when he looked through his passenger side rear view mirror, he saw a man (ronald) laying on the ground. toven exited his vehicle to check on ronald who told him what he was trying to sleep something off. toven then called 911 for assistance. it should be noted that toven does not know ronald and are not related. ronald was found about 21ft east (inside the property) from the sidewalk but it appeared, [roadway] evidence/skid mark, that ronald was initially sleeping under a tree, located inside the property ([roadway]) about 8ft east from the sidewalk, with his legs extending out to the driveway. there was a kool box of cigarettes laying on the ground near by the tree where the skid mark began. ronald claimed that the cigarettes were his and that he was laying there. the skid mark was not from braking but rather from loose gravel and blue jeans fabric (what ronald was currently wearing). the length of the skid mark was 13ft indicating that ronald/foot was ran over and dragged. ofc. v. gonzalez also located an empty bottle of wine (sutter home chardonnay) about 15 ft north from the driveway entrance. it should be noted that there is a retaining wall and multiple trees at the entrance of the driveway making difficult to see anything or anyone laying or sitting down from a moving vehicle [medical facility].
